metadata.content: Oleksandr Usyk's manager dismisses Tyson Fury's offer to be 'backup plan' for Anthony Joshua fight amid doubt over heavyweight clash | Boxing News | Sky Sports Skip to content Oleksandr Usyk's manager dismisses Tyson Fury's offer to be 'backup plan' for Anthony Joshua fight amid doubt over heavyweight clash A long-awaited heavyweight fight between Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua has been stuck in negotiations in recent months amid an apparent disagreement over the location for the proposed clash in November; Fury called out Oleksandr Usyk on Monday Monday 7 September 2026 21:26, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Tyson Fury calls out Oleksandr Usyk in a social media video after claiming Anthony Joshua will never fight the Gypsy King Oleksandr Usyk's manager has dismissed Tyson Fury's call for a third fight with the Ukrainian amid continued doubt over an all-British heavyweight showdown with Anthony Joshua. With protracted negotiations over a long-awaited Fury-Joshua bout being held up by a dispute over where the fight would take place, Fury took to social media on Monday to say he was looking for a new opponent. Fury said he wants a third fight with Usyk, who became undisputed heavyweight champion as he beat Fury twice on points in 2024. messages.text: Zheng stages epic comeback to reach US Open quarters after Swiatek implodes

metadata.summary: Qinwen Zheng staged a second epic comeback at the US Open in as many days to stun former champion Iga Swiatek and book her place in the quarter-finals for the third time.
metadata.content: US Open 2026: Qinwen Zheng stages epic comeback to stun Iga Swiatek and reach quarter-finals | Tennis News | Sky Sports Skip to content US Open 2026: Qinwen Zheng stages epic comeback to stun Iga Swiatek and reach quarter-finals Qinwen Zheng produces another stunning fightback to knock out former champion Iga Swiatek and reach the US Open quarter-finals; Mirra Andreeva also through to last eight with comeback win over Anastasia Potapova; watch the US Open live on Sky Sports Tennis Monday 7 September 2026 19:47, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of Iga Swiatek's match against Qinwen Zheng at the US Open Qinwen Zheng staged a second epic comeback at the US Open in as many days to stun former champion Iga Swiatek and book her place in the quarter-finals for the third time. Two days on from saving match point while trailing 5-0 in the third set to Madison Keys, Zheng mounted another remarkable fightback on Arthur Ashe. Swiatek won the first five games but Zheng simply refused to roll over, winning the next seven games to clinch the first set before overpowering her shellshocked opponent to complete an astonishing 7-5 6-3 victory. A stunned Swiatek never recovered, and the 2022 champion succumbed in straight sets, 7-5 6-3, leaving the court in tears after her campaign unravelled in unthinkable fashion. metadata.summary: Isack Hadjar will miss this weekend's Spanish Grand Prix in Madrid as he continues to recover from a fractured wrist.
metadata.content: Isack Hadjar to miss Spanish Grand Prix in Madrid due to wrist injury as Liam Lawson continues at Red Bull | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to content Isack Hadjar to miss Spanish Grand Prix in Madrid due to wrist injury as Liam Lawson continues at Red Bull Red Bull confirm Isack Hadjar will miss a third straight race due to his ongoing wrist injury; Liam Lawson replaces him as Max Verstappen's team-mate again; watch every session of the Spanish Grand Prix at a new track in Madrid from this Friday, live on Sky Sports F1 Nigel Chiu Sports Journalist @NigelCJourno Monday 7 September 2026 18:36, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Craig Slater reveals further details about Isack Hadjar's injury ahead of the Dutch GP. Isack Hadjar will miss this weekend's Spanish Grand Prix in Madrid as he continues to recover from a fractured wrist. Liam Lawson will replace Hadjar for a third successive race as Max Verstappen's team-mate at Red Bull, while Yuki Tsunoda continues at Racing Bulls. Hadjar suffered a hairline fracture in a bone in his wrist during the summer break in a routine workout that involved boxing which forced him to miss the Dutch, Italian and now Spanish Grands Prix. messages.text: Leicester have sunk to new low under Martin but can he turn it around?

metadata.summary: A decade ago in September 2016, Leicester City were getting ready to play in the Champions League.
metadata.content: Leicester City sink to new low in League One but can Russell Martin turn it around? | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to content Leicester City sink to new low in League One but can Russell Martin turn it around? Leicester City find themselves sat 17th in League One after an embarrassing 4-0 home defeat against Oxford United on Saturday; Russell Martin is already under pressure after just one win in their first five games. Monday 7 September 2026 15:14, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Can Russell Martin turn Leicester's fortunes around after a poor start to the season in League One - here's what the EFL Show panel think. A decade ago in September 2016, Leicester City were getting ready to play in the Champions League. Now? They sit 17th in League One, the lowest position in the club's history since they entered the Football League in 1894. Russell Martin has led the Foxes to just one win in their first five games, and on Saturday they were battered 4-0 at home by Oxford United. Leicester fans were chanting 'you're getting sacked in the morning' at Martin at the King Power Stadium, who would have been desperate for a good start to turn his reputation around after a dismal end to his time at Southampton, and then a gruelling spell at Rangers. On a track where very low tyre degradation used to generate long periods of a train of cars simply following each other, this was relentless overtaking and counter-attack. And of course, the fairytale victory of Italian hero Kimi Antonelli who went from 19th on the grid into the lead just 18 laps later. metadata.summary: Mimi Rhodes is relishing the chance to fulfil a childhood dream at the Solheim Cup and is backing Anna Nordqvist to lead Team Europe to victory in the Netherlands.
metadata.content: Solheim Cup: Mimi Rhodes ready to fulfil childhood dream for Team Europe and backs Anna Nordqvist's side for home win | Golf News | Sky Sports Skip to content Exclusive Solheim Cup: Mimi Rhodes ready to fulfil childhood dream for Team Europe and backs Anna Nordqvist's side for home win Team Europe look to regain Solheim Cup from Team USA at Bernardus Golf this week; Mimi Rhodes one of four rookies in Anna Nordqvist's side chasing home win in the Netherlands; watch the opening day live on Friday from 6am on Sky Sports Golf Ali Stafford Senior Sports Journalist Monday 7 September 2026 15:35, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Take a look back at some classic winning moments from the Solheim Cup archives Mimi Rhodes is relishing the chance to fulfil a childhood dream at the Solheim Cup and is backing Anna Nordqvist to lead Team Europe to victory in the Netherlands. Rhodes makes her Solheim Cup debut for Team Europe this week at Bernardus Golf, having been named among Nordqvist's captain's picks last month, where the hosts look to regain the trophy after their 2024 defeat to Team USA. The Englishwoman enjoyed a strong amateur career before claiming three wins during her Ladies European Tour rookie season last year, with Rhodes now looking to build on her maiden LPGA Tour campaign by achieving a lifelong goal of representing Europe.
